questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Peru?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Peru article.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Peru on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Peru on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Peru?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Peru on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Peru article.

questions.proof: Peru is bordered to the north by Ecuador and Colombia, to the east by Brazil, to the south by Chile, and to the southeast by Bolivia.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Peru about 1,285,216 square kilometres; France about 643,801 square kilometres; Spain about 505,990 square kilometres; Italy about 302,068 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Lima?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Peru is Lima.
